_comment: Copy this file to stories/<your-id>.json, fill it in, then add a matching entry to stories/manifest.json. Delete the _comment fields when you're done. Every node id referenced ('target', 'goodTarget', 'badTarget', and each character's 'starts' values) must match a key in 'nodes'. There are three kinds of node: a scene (has 'choices'), a dice/chance node (has 'roll'), and an ending (has "ending": true).
title: Your Story Title
intro: One or two sentences shown on the character-select screen. Set the scene and the stakes.
_modes_comment: OPTIONAL. 'modes' lets the player replay the same scenario under different conditions, switched from the orange dropdown in the top bar. Each character then needs a 'starts' map with one entry node per mode. Omit 'modes' entirely (and give each character a single 'start' instead of 'starts') for a one-mode story.

modes.label: Base Scenario
modes.description: Face it with the resources you have on hand.

modes.label: Community Involvement & Support
modes.description: The same scenario, but your community or outside support shows up to help.

modes.label: Proactive Risk Resilience
modes.description: Invest in a resilience measure before the scenario plays out, then live with the results.

characters.name: Character A Name
characters.description: What this character knows, cares about, and is up against.

characters.name: Character B Name
characters.description: What this character knows, cares about, and is up against.

a_start.title: Scene heading (optional)
a_start.text:
Scene text. Use a blank line

to split paragraphs. (You can also use an array of strings instead.)

choices.text: A choice that leads to a dice roll.
Second choice the player can make.

a_chance._comment: A DICE / CHANCE NODE. The player clicks an animated die. If it lands on one of 'badFaces', they go to 'badTarget' (the risk happens); otherwise they go to 'goodTarget'. Use this for compounding hazards — a flood, high winds, an aftershock — that may or may not strike.
a_chance.title: Compounding Risk (optional heading)
a_chance.text: Describe the risk and what's at stake before the roll.

roll.prompt: Click the die. If it lands on a 2 or a 4, the risk hits.
roll.goodText: Shown when the roll is safe.
roll.badText: Shown when the bad thing happens.

a_good_ending.title: Ending heading
a_good_ending.text: Wrap up this path. 'outcome' may be: "success", "mixed", or "failure" — it controls the colored badge.

a_bad_ending.title: Ending heading
a_bad_ending.text: A different ending for the other choice.

a_start_community._comment: Character A's opening for the Community mode. Same situation as a_start, but help is available — branch from here however you like (you can also point choices back into shared nodes).
a_start_community.title: Community mode opening
a_start_community.text: Character A's scene when the community shows up.

a_start_proactive._comment: Character A's opening for the Proactive mode. Usually starts with a choice of resilience measure to implement BEFORE the scenario, then runs the scenario with that advantage.
a_start_proactive.title: Proactive mode opening
a_start_proactive.text: Character A invests in resilience before the event, then faces it.

b_start.title: Scene heading
b_start.text: Character B's opening scene. (This character points every mode at the same start node — a valid choice when a character's story doesn't change between modes.)
